title: Is China Getting Involved in the Japan-Russia Territorial Dispute?
gist: A Heilongjiang delegation visited Russian-controlled Iturup Island, prompting Japan's protest and raising the question of coordinated China-Russia pressure on Japan over the Northern Territories (truncated excerpt).

insights.claim: Per Russia's Sakhalin Oblast government on October 13, a delegation of officials and entrepreneurs from China's Heilongjiang Province visited Iturup Island (Etorofu), part of the Southern Kurils under Russian de facto control but claimed by Japan.
insights.speaker: Zhenlin Cui
insights.so_what: Chinese commercial engagement in disputed islands signals deeper China-Russia regional ties.

insights.claim: Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu called the visit 'absolutely unacceptable'.
insights.speaker: Zhenlin Cui
insights.so_what: Japan-China tension adds to a troubled bilateral relationship.

insights.claim: Beijing responded that it consistently advocates respecting the outcomes of the WWII victory, and a Japanese media outlet suggested this reflects a coordinated China-Russia stance and joint approach toward Japan.
insights.speaker: Zhenlin Cui
insights.so_what: Possible alignment of Beijing and Moscow against Tokyo; treat as speculative.
